title: "Giovannino tai kuolema!"
summary: "Giovannino tai kuolema!" by Matilde Serao is a novella written in the early 20th century. Set in Naples, it follows the fierce young Chiarina, her domineering moneylender stepmother donna Gabriella, and the tender but cautious Giovannino, weighing love against poverty, pride, and the temptations of easy gain. With sharp social observation, it portrays crowded tenement life, the public gaze of neighbors, and the moral shadows cast by a pawnshop economy. The opening of the novella unfolds on a Pentecost Sunday around the S.S. Apostoli church, briskly sketching the tenants of a grimy Neapolitan building: harried families, a complacent childless couple, a pedantic ex-official and his wife, students, and servants. Amid the hubbub, donna Gabriella bullies Chiarina over clothes and her attachment to Giovannino, prompting the girl’s defiant cry, “Giovannino or death,” and a slap that the whole house hears. After mass, Chiarina and Giovannino speak across the courtyard well, debating elopement versus the need for money, and he resolves to petition the stepmother. To Chiarina’s shock, donna Gabriella receives him kindly and consents to the match, drawing warm support from the neighbors; supervised visits follow, while discreet signals pass under the window at night. Soon, though, troubling signs appear: lavish linens arrive from the pawnshop, their origin tainting Chiarina’s joy; she learns they must live under donna Gabriella’s roof; Giovannino grows evasive about work and increasingly absorbed in the “office” (the pawn business), trading advice and ledgers with the stepmother. The section closes as an anguished Chiarina, feeling her love pulled into that moral fog, asks to speak with Giovannino alone. (This is an automatically generated summary.)
